first_impression.reaction: My assistant found it while pulling together florals notes for a Sydney date. The first screen is calm and sensible, no 'dream bouquet', no prices, no discounts. It reads like quiet advice, which I prefer. But it is written for a couple sitting down with one local florist, not a family dressing several spaces for 300 guests. Her summary would be 'season follows the date, ask what is local, what is imported and what the backup is, abroad use a florist at the destination'. I read the takeaways, the in-season or imported section, the destination section and the close. I skimmed the months.

journey.quote: Choosing wedding flowers in season starts with a date, not a mood board.
journey.reaction: Good opening. Confident, not eager. I would keep reading.

journey.section: Why choose wedding flowers in season
journey.quote: Petals hold their shape, stems drink well, and arrangements last through a long evening rather than tiring by the speeches.
journey.reaction: This is the only thing I actually care about with flowers: they must look right at midnight, not just at the ceremony. Said simply.

journey.section: Winter in June, July and August
journey.quote: Ask about scale too: in a smaller winter room, a few generous arrangements can carry more presence than many small ones.
journey.reaction: The only mention of scale on the page, and it is about a small room. Nothing about what changes when you need flowers for 30 tables, a ceremony, a reception and a second event the next day.

journey.quote: Some couples find that the flower they have always pictured is simply not grown in Australia in their wedding month.
journey.reaction: This is my situation exactly. If I want a particular flower, it will be flown in. Good that it is treated as reasonable, not frowned on.

journey.quote: - **What is imported?** Which stems will come from overseas, and when they need to be ordered.
journey.reaction: Right question, but at our volume the lead time is the whole problem. It should say that a large order changes the timing.

journey.quote: Agree in writing which flowers are essential to you and which the florist may substitute.
journey.reaction: Sensible. My assistant would copy this into the brief.

journey.quote: Resist the urge to pack flowers from home.
journey.reaction: Nobody in my family was going to pack flowers. It reads as written for someone doing it themselves.

journey.quote: Share your date and venue with them early, along with a few images of the mood you are after rather than a list of stems.
journey.reaction: Mood rather than a stem list is the right instinct. But a florist needs to know the guest count and how many spaces are being dressed, and that is missing.

journey.section: Planning your flowers and spend with your florist
journey.quote: With Wedded Concierge, you have one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact, and your advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One contact suits me: fewer people, fewer leaks. Nothing tells me they have handled my scale, though.

journey.section: Plan your flowers with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, so the flowers sit within a plan that already fits your date and your destination.
journey.reaction: Understated, no package talk. Fine. But a florals post is not where I would judge a planner.

unanswered_questions: Have you delivered florals for a wedding of 200 to 400 guests across several events, and can you show one discreetly? (deferred business detail)
Which florists would you put forward for us, in Sydney or abroad, and how are they chosen? (deferred business detail: sourcing and vetting)
How is the Wedded Advisor paid, and is anything earned from the florist? (deferred business detail: fees and commissions)
Can a florist at our scale bring their own team into an exclusive-use venue days ahead, and who keeps staff phones and social media in check during set-up?
How far ahead do imported stems need ordering when the quantity is very large?

turn_offs_found.quote: Resist the urge to pack flowers from home.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. It assumes the reader is carrying their own flowers in a suitcase, which lowers the register for a family whose suppliers handle this.

would_share_with: My assistant would keep the three questions (local, imported, backup) and the 'agree in writing' line for the florals brief. Nobody else.

cta_reaction.why: I don't enquire through a blog link, and a florals guide is not where I choose a planner. The tone did not put me off, which is more than most of these pages manage. I would still want a private introduction and some sign they have worked at our size.

top_3_changes: Acknowledge scale in the July note so a large wedding sees itself. OLD: "Ask about scale too: in a smaller winter room, a few generous arrangements can carry more presence than many small ones." NEW: "Ask about scale too: in a smaller winter room, a few generous arrangements can carry more presence than many small ones, and for a large guest list or several events across a weekend, ask how the florist will staff the set-up of every space."

Flag lead time for big orders in the imported question. OLD: "- **What is imported?** Which stems will come from overseas, and when they need to be ordered." NEW: "- **What is imported?** Which stems will come from overseas, when they need to be ordered, and whether a large quantity changes that lead time."

Give the destination florist the facts they need, and drop the suitcase line. OLD: "Share your date and venue with them early, along with a few images of the mood you are after rather than a list of stems." NEW: "Share your date, venue, guest count and the spaces to be dressed with them early, along with a few images of the mood you are after rather than a list of stems." Also OLD: "Resist the urge to pack flowers from home. Every country sets its own rules on bringing in plant material, and a florist at the destination can build the look you want from what is already there." NEW: "Every country sets its own rules on bringing in plant material, so a florist at the destination is best placed to build the look you want from what is already there."

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Layla (uhnw): assistant-first skim, judged from the first screen, looked for scale, privacy and understated tone, put off by over-explaining
No invented brand facts; scale proof, florist sourcing and vetting, fees and commissions listed in unanswered_questions as deferred
Suggested edits stay within brand limits: no named flowers, no fees, commissions, sourcing or vetting claims; exact old/new strings given
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Layla's main gap is scale: the draft never addresses large guest counts or multi-event weekends. The suggested edits are reader-side questions only and add no brand or flower claims. Weigh against the 0.20 persona weight and the post's mass-market keyword.

Persona is provisional and not CRM-calibrated, so confidence is 0.75.
